newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-ICI puts bought in dividend arbitrage deal.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-ICI puts bought in dividend arbitrage deal.

text.p: Stock market weakness ahead of the weekend took its toll on the equity options market and business merely trickled through on Friday, dealers said.
A dividend-related deal in Imperial Chemical Industries was one of the biggest trades by mid-afternoon.
It involved buying 2,000 April 950 puts at 224p against buying two million ICI shares at 750p, making a net debit of 974p per share.
The stock will go ex-dividend on Monday by 24.25p gross (19.4p net) so the stock can be sold at 950p after that date by exercisng the puts and still collect the dividend.
Using the gross dividend amount, the net credit will then be 974.25p -- making a locked-in overall guaranteed profit of 0.25p per share or 500,000 stg in total before costs.
By 1525 GMT, ICI shares had fallen 3-1/2p to 753p.
In gas services company Centrica, the main deal in volume terms was from a seller of 1,000 March 50 puts at 1/2p. The underlying shares shed 2p to 66-1/4p.
And in food retailer J Sainsbury, the main deal was the purchase of 250 April 330 calls at 5-1/2p.
Also bullish was the deal in insurer Commercial Union where 425 April 700 calls were bought at 15p.
Elsewhere, oil major Shell Transport & Trading was wanted by one trader who bought 500 April 1050 calls at 22p.
Sainsbury slipped 4p to 308-1/2p, Commercial Union added a penny to 678-1/2p and Shell succumbed 9-1/2 to 1044p.

Over in index options, calls spreads hedged by FTSE futures were popular. The biggest deal involved the sale of 1,000 March 4350 FTSE 100 calls and the purchase of 1,000 March 4400 calls for a net credit of 17-1/2p against buying March futures at 4312. By 1525 GMT, spot FTSE was down 24.0 at 4315.2 and March futures were down 42 at 4288.
